Maya Patel: Quick follow-up on the token storm last night — observed auth provider token refresh spikes that correlated with 502/503s from model-registry proxied requests in eu-west. Root cause looks like concurrent refreshes for many short-lived tokens.
Ajay Singh: yep saw the same in traces. lots of `401 -> refresh -> race -> 429` from the registry side.
Sarah Li: timeline? when did the spike start/stop?
Maya Patel: Started 02:13 UTC, peaked 02:17, mitigated by autoscaling at 02:29, full tail ended ~03:05. Impacted hosted inference routes + a few Dedicated pools routing through the same auth gateway.
Kevin O'Connor: Vendor (AuthCorp) throttle policy kicked in; they returned `429` to our refresh endpoint. I've opened a support ticket (AUTH-9182) asking for detailed logs and a temporary throttle increase.
Jen Park: quick mitigation ideas: bump local token cache TTL from 60s -> 300s, add jitter to refresh, and add an async refresh queue to serialize refreshes per subject.
Ajay Singh: agree. hotfix plan: 1) cache TTL change + client-side dedupe 2) retry/backoff on 429 3) monitor errors. Can push a 1-line config change to our secrets agent and roll. Low risk.
Maya Patel: owners and timelines proposed: 
- Hotfix (24h): Ajay (token cache & dedupe) + Jen (integration tests)
- Short-term (2w): Sarah (runbook updates, alerts, add aggregate metric for concurrent refreshes), Kevin (vendor response + SLA ask)
- Long-term (8w): Ajay + EngRuntime (signed-request relay / fallback auth path), Product (policy for token TTL defaults)
Sarah Li: I'll take runbook + alerts. I'll add an alert `auth.refresh_concurrency > 50 for 3m` and a dashboard panel.
Kevin O'Connor: I'll push vendor follow-up and request a temporary throttle increase and logs. If we don't hear in 48h, escalate to channel partner.
Jen Park: Can validate behavioral tests in staging. I'll add a regression test that simulates N clients refreshing in the same second.
Maya Patel: low-level guardrails: add short-circuit so if auth refresh fails with 429 we serve cached token for up to 60s before forcing a hard fail. That reduces burst reauth loops.
Ajay Singh: sample config I'm going to deploy: 
```
secrets_agent:
  token_cache_ttl: 300
  refresh_jitter_ms: 250-1000
  dedupe_window_ms: 5000
retries:
  on_429: exponential_backoff(initial=200ms, max=5s, attempts=5)
```
Kevin O'Connor: question — does increasing TTL risk longer exposure if a token is revoked? we should add a short revocation listener/flag.
Maya Patel: good call. we'll wire the revocation hook to invalidate cache immediately (short-term task for Ajay).
incidents-bot: Reminder created: "Auth token storm mitigation - hotfix due" due in 24 hours. Assigned: Ajay Singh, Jen Park.
deploy-bot: Noted: config patch `secrets_agent.token_cache_ttl` queued in canary. CI checks passing.
Sarah Li: I'll update the postmortem follow-up doc with the owners and timelines: https://redwood.company/docs/incidents/auth-token-storm-followup (draft).
Jen Park: I'll pair with Ajay for the staging run tomorrow 09:30 PT.
Maya Patel: OK — action items recap (short): 
- Ajay: push cache TTL + dedupe hotfix (24h) + revocation hook (48h)
- Jen: test harness + staging run (24-48h)
- Sarah: runbook + alert + postmortem doc edits (2w)
- Kevin: vendor escalation + SLA/logs (48h)
incidents-bot: Follow-up reminder scheduled for 2 weeks to verify short-term items and runbook adoption.
Kevin O'Connor: +1 on timelines. I'll also ask legal to check SLA language for throttle exceptions.
Maya Patel: thanks all. We'll re-check tomorrow after canary. Please add any blockers in-thread. :eyes: :calendar: 
Ajay Singh: ACK, starting work now.
Sarah Li: ACK and will post updated alert ID when ready. :thumbsup:
